title: From Latent to Observable Position-Based Click Models in Carousel Interfaces

problem.claim: Click models are central to learning and evaluating recommender systems.

gap.claim: Most existing click models are designed for single ranked list interfaces, while modern platforms increasingly use carousel interfaces with multiple swipeable lists and complex browsing behaviors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Click models are central to recommender-system learning and evaluation.
Modern recommender platforms increasingly use carousels, creating browsing behaviors not represented by models designed for single ranked lists.

source_observation.claim: A change from single ranked lists to multiple swipeable lists introduces more complex user browsing behaviors.

interpretation.claim: Modeling assumptions should account for the interaction structure of the interface.

application.claim: Evaluate whether recommender-system click models represent the interface structures in which users interact.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish how such interface-aware modeling should be implemented or when it is necessary.

unknowns: The abstract units do not state the paper's method, theoretical results, experiments, datasets, or findings.
The abstract units do not explicitly state a novel contribution.
